notes: All HVS-named entries in the roster are follow_up: T:p13-b7 distinguishes the B-named objects as those originally considered bound, while T:p14-b2 explicitly refers back to the stars originally considered unbound; T:p2-b6 confirms that 40 MMT outliers were analyzed. HVS 11, HVS 14, and HVS 23 are retained even though proper motions were unavailable (T:p8-b7). HVS 2 and HVS 3 are mentioned only as literature context and are not analyzed targets. Newly identified unbound candidates: B095, B129, B329, and B458 lie in the 19-object unconstrained group (T:p9-b14; I:p10-b0), for which the paper reports bound probabilities below 50% except for B1080 (T:p9-b14; I:p18-b0). B481 and B1085 lie in the eight-object outer-rim group (T:p10-b3; I:p12-b0), where only B167, B434, and B711 exceed 50% bound probability and most of the group is likely unbound (T:p11-b2; I:p18-b0). B485 is included on the explicit conditional statement that it would likely be unbound in Model II (T:p13-b8; I:p19-b0). B1080 is excluded because its quoted bound probability is 67% (T:p9-b14; I:p18-b0). B167, B434, and B711 are excluded because their bound probabilities exceed 50% (T:p11-b2). B576 and B598 are excluded because their main-sequence-only unbound possibilities are not retained; the preferred BHB/pre-ELM solutions are bound (T:p11-b12, T:p12-b2, T:p11-b11; I:p18-b0). B143, B537, B572, B733, and B1139 are excluded as reported bound, disk-origin objects (I:p18-b0). HVS 24's SDSS alias is recorded as SDSSJ111336.44+005856.4 from the Table 4 image (I:p7-b0); the text transcription appears to omit a digit. No Gaia source identifiers are printed in the supplied material.

HVS 1: Target: HVS 1 (SDSSJ090744.99+024506.8). Table 1 separates random/statistical and systematic radial-velocity uncertainties; they are reported separately rather than combined. The distance is the spectrophotometric distance from Table 4, not a Gaia parallax distance. The paper states that Gaia DR2 proper motions were used for the kinematic analysis but does not tabulate right ascension, declination, parallax, or proper motions for individual stars, so those quantities are omitted. Galactic rest-frame velocity and bound probability are from the kinematic tables and depend on the adopted Galactic potential; values for both Model I and Model II are given where identical. Galactocentric radius is not tabulated directly (only Cartesian x, y, z and plane-crossing quantities are listed), so it is omitted rather than calculated.

HVS 4: HVS 4 is listed as SDSSJ091301.01+305119.8 in Table 4 (I:p7-b0). The paper does not tabulate individual RA, Dec, parallax, or proper-motion components for this star; it only states generally that Gaia DR2 proper motions were used. Only bound probability P_b is reported, so no unbound probability is recorded. No current galactocentric radius r is listed; Table A.1 gives Cartesian x, y, z (I:p18-b0), which was not used to calculate r. Table 1 reports radial-velocity statistical and systematic errors separately; the stored errors are statistical, and the systematic component is given in the condition.

HVS 5: RA and Dec are parsed from the SDSS J2000 designation SDSSJ091759.47+672238.3 in Table 4 (T:p7-b0); the paper does not tabulate an independent astrometric position for HVS 5. No parallax or proper-motion components are tabulated for HVS 5. No present-day galactocentric radius is explicitly tabulated; Tables A.1 and A.2 give x, y, z and the plane-crossing r_p, so no galactocentric_radius value was extracted. In T:p11-b10, the phrase 'ejection velocity of v_Grf = 670^{+80}_{-60} km/s' is inconsistent with Table A.1, where 670^{+80}_{-60} km/s is v_ej,p; the present-day v_Grf is 650^{+10}_{-20} km/s.
